thread:
lisa_support: Escalation from Acme — streaming responses sometimes show up as 5xx on our side but the customer says the model produced the final tokens and client disconnected. They're disputing billing for those requests. Example request_id: req-7f9e3b2a. Customer says they received a 502 in the SDK, but server logs show backend streamed chunks and "finished". Need help triaging.
adarsh_oncall: Can you paste the gateway logs for req-7f9e3b2a? Also any customer repro steps or curl they used.
lisa_support: Pasted excerpt below (redacted IPs):
```
2026-02-20T18:11:34Z gateway INFO req=req-7f9e3b2a method=POST path=/v1/streams model=gpt-large client_ip=1.2.3.4
2026-02-20T18:11:34Z proxy DEBUG req=req-7f9e3b2a upstream_conn=pool-12 acquired
2026-02-20T18:11:36Z upstream INFO req=req-7f9e3b2a backend_status=200 bytes_sent=12345 stream_done=true
2026-02-20T18:11:36Z gateway WARN req=req-7f9e3b2a write_error=EPIPE client_close=true mapped_status=502 billing_flag=5xx_counted
```
Customer's repro (from James):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \ 
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams -d @payload.json
# payload.json has a few small chunks and then client closes the connection shortly after receiving the final chunk
```
They say the client closed connection after consuming the last chunk, and their SDK surfaced a 502/5xx. They argue we should not bill them for those as server completed successfully.
mike_sre: Hmm. Log shows upstream reported stream_done=true and backend_status=200, then gateway saw a client-side write error EPIPE and set mapped_status=502. We currently increment our 5xx counter when the gateway write path returns an error. That means a client disconnect can be classified as a 5xx for billing/alerts.
adarsh_oncall: Repro steps I used locally to simulate the problem:
```
# start a tiny HTTP server that responds with chunked encoding and sleeps between chunks
python -c "from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer; import time; 
class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
  def do_POST(self):
    self.send_response(200)
    self.send_header('Transfer-Encoding','chunked')
    self.end_headers()
    for i in range(3):
      chunk = ('chunk-%d\n' % i).encode()
      self.wfile.write(hex(len(chunk))[2:].encode()+b"\r\n"+chunk+b"\r\n")
      self.wfile.flush(); time.sleep(1)
    self.wfile.write(b"0\r\n\r\n")

HTTPServer(('127.0.0.1',8000),H).serve_forever()"

# client: read two chunks and then kill the process to simulate consumer abort
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:8000/ -d @payload.json &
sleep 2; pkill -f "curl -N"
```
When I kill the client right after the server sends the last chunk, the server logs indicate success but the proxy observes an EPIPE and our gateway increments a 502 counter.
mike_sre: Root cause hypothesis: our billing/metrics middleware currently determines success/failure solely from the gateway-level final write result. If the backend wrote successfully but the TCP write to client fails (client closed first), we still mark the whole request as a 5xx because the write path returned an error. That causes both alerts and billing increment.
tasha_billing: If that is true, customers will see unexpected 5xx billing hits. We need a rule: do not increment billable 5xx when backend_status is 2xx and backend_stream_done=true and bytes_sent>0 and close_reason is client_abort. Instead, classify as client_abort/499-like and exclude from billing. We'll need a clear definition for accounting.
adarsh_oncall: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: treat mapped_status=502 with upstream_status=200 and write_error=EPIPE as non-billable. I'll push a routing rule to the gateway for the next deploy window to stop counting those. Long-term: fix the status mapping so gateway reports 499/CLIENT_ABORT and doesn’t increment 5xx meter when upstream succeeded.
lisa_support: Can we also run a retroactive query to find customers affected (last 30 days) and surface candidates for credits? James from Acme needs an immediate reply.
mike_sre: Query I ran: COUNT(*) where billing_flag=5xx_counted and upstream_status=200 and write_error is not null between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-20 -> ~4200 requests across 7 customers. I'll attach the top account ids.
adarsh_oncall: Action items:
- (P0) Add temporary non-bill rule for mapped_status=502 + upstream_status=200 + write_error like EPIPE (adarsh) — deploy in next 2 hours
- (P1) Patch gateway: introduce explicit client-abort status (499) and change billing middleware to use upstream_status when available (mike)
- (P1) Add unit/integration test covering chunked streaming + client aborts (adarsh + eng-runtime)
- (P2) Billing review & credits (tasha)
- (P3) Customer comms (lisa)
deploy-bot: Scheduled deployment window: 2026-02-20T20:00Z -> jobs queued: gateway-rule-2026-02-20
tasha_billing: I'll prepare a credit proposal. For customers with >100 aborts in timeframe we'll issue a manual credit equal to average token spend for similar non-aborted requests. Need exact list from SRE.
lisa_support: James — we can offer Acme a credit and an explanation: we discovered that client-side disconnects after the backend finished could be misclassified as 5xx and listed on metrics/billing. We're fixing classification and will issue a retro credit for affected calls. We'll follow up with estimated credit amount within 24 hours. :white_check_mark:
james_acme_customer: Thanks — appreciate the quick response. Please let me know if you need a HAR or SDK trace from our side. We can reproduce consistently with small chunk sizes and a client disconnect after final chunk.
mike_sre: Request for follow-up logs if needed: please include request_id header, client local IP (so we can match), and time window. We'll correlate. Also attaching proposed code diff for billing middleware (pseudo):
```
if upstream_status and upstream_status < 500:
  mark_non_billable()
elif gateway_error and not upstream_status:
  mark_billable()
else:
  fallback_old_behavior()
```
